        """

        self.directory = directory

        self.config_filename = os.path.join(directory, "config.json")
        with open(self.config_filename, encoding = "utf8") as f:

        if kwargs.get("st_variants"):
            self.stc = VariantSafetensorsCollection(kwargs.get("st_variants"))

        # Collect all .safetensors files in directory
        else:
            self.stc = SafetensorsCollection(directory, load_method = kwargs.get("load_method"))

        self.bos_token_id = self.read_cfg(int, "bos_token_id", None)
        self.eos_token_id = self.read_cfg([int, list], "eos_token_id", None)
        self.pad_token_id = self.read_cfg(int, "pad_token_id", None)
        self.vocab_size = self.read_cfg(int, ["vocab_size", "text_config->vocab_size"], None)
        if isinstance(self.eos_token_id, list):

            self.eos_token_id = self.eos_token_id[0]
        else:
            self.eos_token_id_list = [self.eos_token_id]

        # Standard params, unused

        self.head_dim = -1
        self.num_q_heads = -1
        self.num_kv_heads = -1

            if value != no_value and value != expected_value:

  },
  "objects": [
    {
      "author_login": "oobabooga",
      "content": "I have quantized [deepcogito/cogito-v1-preview-qwen-32B](https://huggingface.co/deepcogito/cogito-v1-preview-qwen-32B) for tests, and found that the following bpw worked perfectly, with no noticeable performance degradation:\n\n* 3.0bpw\n* 4.0bpw\n* 5.0bpw\n* 6.0bpw\n* 8.0bpw\n\nHowever, the following bpw are completely incoherent:\n\n* 2.0bpw\n* 2.25bpw\n* 2.5bpw\n\nThey output random non-latin characters for every input I have tried.\n\nI have uploaded these models here: https://huggingface.co/oobabooga/cogito-v1-preview-qwen-32B-exl3",
      "content_sha256": "6f5952a0100e2a84b29ba02b2b29189e710d94529edc6e2958442b34fc1f4a6b",
      "created_at": "2025-04-15T17:02:04Z",

      "source_id": "I_kwDOOU24Gs6yo6eP",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/issues/15"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "turboderp",
      "content": "So I've spent the past couple of days investigating this, and I'm no closer to a real answer. There's something very strange about a few specific tensors in the model and they just don't want to quantize correctly below 3 bpw with the normal regularization scheme. It also seems to affect QwQ-32B.\n\nI'll figure it out eventually, but in the meantime I've added a workaround that tries to detect when the full regularization is actually needed and disables the output channel normalization otherwise, which seems to have done the trick, and I'm able to quantize it at 2 bpw. Sadly it does mean the broken versions need to be converted again.",
      "content_sha256": "340194f432e98b5f8a8a882469e0124f0471a95c241e68068df15d657cf9d427",
      "created_at": "2025-04-17T17:56:56Z",

      "source_id": "IC_kwDOOU24Gs6ntUKU",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/issues/15#issuecomment-2813674132"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "oobabooga",
      "content": "Thanks for looking into this. Having to reconvert some broken or sub-optimal quants is entirely expected with EXL3 at such an early stage.\n\nI don't know if it helps at all, but I put this issue in a long conversation I had with Claude a few days ago (where I was trying to understand how EXL3 works by looking at its source code), and the model brought up\n\n```python\n    diag = H_diag.sqrt()  # Square root of diagonal elements of Hessian\n    cv = diag.std() / diag.mean()  # Coefficient of variation\n    apply_out_scales = cv < threshold  # e.g., threshold = 1.0\n```\n\nas a possible alternative to\n\n```python\n    diag = H_diag.sqrt()\n    diag, _ = torch.sort(diag, descending = True)\n    cutoff = diag.shape[0] // 50\n    skew_factor = diag[:cutoff].sum() / diag.sum()\n    if verbose:\n        print(f\"     - input state skew: {skew_factor.item():.6f}\")\n    \n    if force_out_scales is None:\n        apply_out_scales = skew_factor.item() < 0.15\n    else:\n        apply_out_scales = force_out_scales\n```\n\nusing the \"coefficient of variation (CV) of the Hessian diagonal\".\n\nOf course I have no idea what any of this means, if this improves anything, if there is a more fundamental way to tackle this, but this has 1 parameter istead of 2 so I figured I should share it to see if it gives you any idea.",
